title: Cycle Pulse & Echo: Capacity Canvas and Slate Shepherding
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In high-velocity cycles we repeatedly hit two friction points: (1) teams over-commit early and then scramble to de-scope mid-cycle, and (2) platform ops can't reliably forecast burst capacity needs for Dedicated on short notice. Scope: establish a repeatable lightweight process and artifacts (Capacity Canvas + Slate Shepherd) that combine quantitative capacity budgeting with qualitative tradeoff surfaces so PMs and Eng leads can make deterministic cycle choices. Goals: reduce mid-cycle scope churn by 30%, shorten decision turnaround for staffing reallocations to <48h, and provide a 2-week predictive window for Dedicated capacity requests. Approach: introduce "Pulse" checkpoints (pre-cycle, week2 pulse, mid-cycle pulse) with clear signals and an "Echo" reserve policy (micro-credits pool + shadow roster). Deliverables: (1) Capacity Canvas template (workload-weighted token-hours, critical-path roles, cross-team friction points), (2) Slate Shepherding rubric (decomposition rules, soft/hard deltas, canary gating), (3) Runbook for triggering micro-credit allocations and emergency de-scope flows, (4) Dashboard cards and alert thresholds in Console to show capacity burn and reserve projections. Tradeoffs: simpler heuristics reduce cognitive load but may underfit highly variable infra bursts; we include a small modelling component to flag low-confidence forecasts. Stakeholders: PMs, Eng leads, SRE, People Ops for short-term staffing, Solutions for Dedicated customer communications. Success metrics: mid-cycle scope changes reduced; average time-to-allocate staff from pool; Dedicated capacity requests predicted 2 weeks ahead with >75% accuracy. This ticket covers articulation of templates, decision criteria, small pilot with two initiatives, and tooling hooks for alerts. Links to artifacts and PRs included below.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity Canvas template authored and reviewed by Eng+PM+SRE

Runbook for micro-credit allocation with owner and SLA (<48h) for staff allocation

Pilot run completed on Initiative Alpha and Initiative Beta with post-mortem and metrics
